samples.summary: Share-link Esc test is vacuous — `expect(...).not.toThrow()` passes regardless of behavior
samples.evidence: The test titled "does nothing on Esc for a share-link viewer" only asserts `expect(() => fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: 'Escape' })).not.toThrow()`. Dispatching a keydown never throws to the caller: jsdom catches exceptions raised inside event listeners and reports them as uncaught errors rather than propagating out of `dispatchEvent`. So this assertion holds whether the guard `onClose &&` exists or not, and even if the handler navigated away. It asserts nothing about the claimed behavior ("Esc must stay inert rather than navigate anywhere") — no navigation spy / route-location assertion is made.

samples.summary: Esc test only proves the injected callback fires; the real destination is fully mocked away
samples.evidence: `renderViewer({ onClose })` injects a bare `vi.fn()`, so the test verifies only that the keydown handler invokes its prop. The production `onClose` is `() => navigate(documentsPath)` built in `ImageFileLayout` from `useDocumentsPath`; nothing ties Esc to an actual route change, so a regression in the composed path (wrong workspace slug, missing navigate) would leave this test green.

finding.summary: Share-link Esc test is vacuous — `expect(...).not.toThrow()` passes regardless of behavior
finding.evidence: The test titled "does nothing on Esc for a share-link viewer" only asserts `expect(() => fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: 'Escape' })).not.toThrow()`. Dispatching a keydown never throws to the caller: jsdom catches exceptions raised inside event listeners and reports them as uncaught errors rather than propagating out of `dispatchEvent`. So this assertion holds whether the guard `onClose &&` exists or not, and even if the handler navigated away. verdict.reason: The test at image-viewer.test.tsx:64-67 is exactly as the finding describes: for the share-link viewer (token set, no onClose) it asserts only `expect(() => fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: 'Escape' })).not.toThrow()`. The behavior it claims to cover — Esc staying inert rather than navigating — is implemented at image-viewer.tsx:126 (`else if (e.key === 'Escape' && onClose) onClose();`), but nothing in the test observes it: no navigate spy, no MemoryRouter location assertion, no callback assertion. The handler runs inside window.dispatchEvent, whose listener exceptions jsdom reports rather than propagating, so the assertion holds whether or not the `onClose &&` guard exists; and it would equally pass if the handler navigated away. Sibling tests (lines 45-60) do assert onClose call counts, showing the share-link case uniquely lacks a meaningful assertion. No other test file covers ImageViewer. Vacuous test presented as coverage for a behavior path -> major under the test-adequacy rubric.

Repo-wide case-insensitive grep for 'back to doc' matches only file-detail.tsx:57; grep for 'FileShell|headerLeading' matches only source files; the sole SiteHeader-touching test (tests/app/documents/document-detail-lakehouse-tab.test.tsx:61-62) mocks SiteHeader with a stub that ignores `leading`. finding.evidence: The diff replaces the inline `fallbackSlug` computation with `useDocumentsPath(documentData?.workspaceId)` in the `isDocumentError` redirect effect. verdict.reason: The finding asserts the changed redirect introduces a new semantic (path now prefers the document's own workspace) that has no coverage. Both halves fail. (a) The behavior is guarded: the extracted logic in use-documents-path.ts:19-21 is directly and non-vacuously tested in packages/frontend/src/app/files/__tests__/use-documents-path.test.tsx:28-46, whose first case ("returns the document's own workspace list", :28-32) asserts exactly the semantic claimed uncovered, plus the first-workspace and /documents fallbacks. Only the API module is mocked; the hook logic under test runs for real. (b) There is no semantic change to cover: the pre-refactor inline form survives verbatim in siblings — notes-detail.tsx:76,81, board-detail.tsx:51,56, document-detail.tsx:189,194 — all computing `workspaceSlug ?? workspaces[0]?.slug` where workspaceSlug is already the document's own workspace, i.e. identical output to useDocumentsPath. The task plan states the redirect "reuses it instead of its own copy of the same slug fallback" (todo doc:28-29). I confirmed no test renders FileShell (repo-wide grep for file-shell|FileShell, including packages/frontend/tests/** which the reviewer missed), but the residual untested delta is a one-line navigate() wiring over an input with direct unit coverage — not a behavior change shipped without meaningful test under this lens's rubric.
